title: Anomaly detection: A survey
authors: Chandola, V.; Banerjee, A.; Kumar, V.
method: Survey; taxonomy of anomalies as point/contextual/collective and detection as supervised/semi-supervised/unsupervised
main_findings: Canonical taxonomy of anomaly detection; names the standing difficulties of label rarity, noise, an ill-defined normal/abnormal boundary, and a normal that changes over time
limitations: Pre-dates modern deep and personalized methods; contains no empirical comparison of reference frames
meyro_relevance: Supplies MEYRO's vocabulary for anomaly types and the label-rarity motivation; frames personalization as a reference-frame choice rather than a new algorithm
source_verification: Title, authors, year, venue and DOI confirmed via ACM Digital Library record and author-hosted PDF

title: Isolation Forest
authors: Liu, F.T.; Ting, K.M.; Zhou, Z.-H.
dataset: Benchmark datasets (specific datasets not verified in this pass)
method: Ensemble of random isolation trees; anomaly score derived from expected path length; isolates anomalies instead of profiling normal points
evaluation: AUROC on benchmark datasets (details not verified in this pass)
main_findings: Sub-sampling plus isolation yields high detection accuracy, low memory cost and linear time complexity; anomalies are few and distinct and are therefore isolated early
limitations: Detects globally unusual points; has no temporal or personal reference frame; per-subject behaviour is not modelled
meyro_relevance: Mandatory non-neural comparator for Phase 8 and for the Phase 26 ablation; a temporal model that cannot beat it is not contributing
source_verification: Title, authors, year, venue, pages and DOI confirmed via IEEE Xplore, ACM DL and an author-hosted PDF

title: LSTM-based Encoder-Decoder for Multi-sensor Anomaly Detection
authors: Malhotra, P.; Ramakrishnan, A.; Anand, G.; Vig, L.; Agarwal, P.; Shroff, G.
dataset: ECG and multi-sensor time series (per abstract)
method: Stacked LSTM encoder-decoder (EncDec-AD) trained on normal data only; anomaly score is reconstruction error
main_findings: EncDec-AD is robust across predictable, unpredictable, periodic, aperiodic and quasi-periodic series and detects anomalies from windows as short as 30 steps
limitations: Trained per-series with no explicit personalization mechanism; no false-positive-rate analysis; no population-baseline comparison
meyro_relevance: Template for MEYRO's Phase 9 temporal reconstruction models and for the reconstruction-error deviation score
source_verification: Title, authors, year and arXiv identifier confirmed via arXiv entry 1607.00148; full author list confirmed at abstract level

title: TS2Vec: Towards Universal Representation of Time Series
authors: Yue, Z.; Wang, Y.; Duan, J.; Yang, T.; Huang, C.; Tong, Y.; Xu, B.
dataset: UCR/UEA archives and additional classification, forecasting and anomaly benchmarks (details not verified)
method: Hierarchical contrastive learning over augmented context views producing timestamp-level representations
evaluation: Linear probe and fine-tuning across classification, forecasting and anomaly detection
main_findings: Learns universal representations usable across tasks, at timestamp-level granularity, outperforming prior representation-learning methods
limitations: Pretraining objective is generic and population-level; no per-subject personalization objective; the paper itself does not study health signals
meyro_relevance: Central Phase 12 reference and a fair comparator for the question of whether self-supervision helps a personal baseline at all
source_verification: Title, authors, year, venue and arXiv identifier confirmed via AAAI proceedings and the official implementation repository

title: Simple and Scalable Predictive Uncertainty Estimation using Deep Ensembles
authors: Lakshminarayanan, B.; Pritzel, A.; Blundell, C.
dataset: Regression and classification benchmarks (details not verified)
method: Ensembles of neural networks trained with adversarial perturbation and proper scoring rules

title: A survey on concept drift adaptation
authors: Gama, J.; Zliobaite, I.; Bifet, A.; Pechenizkiy, M.; Bouchachia, A.
method: Taxonomy of drift types (sudden, gradual, incremental, recurring) and of adaptation strategies: windowing, instance weighting, ensembles, explicit drift detectors
main_findings: Concept drift mainly concerns supervised online learning where the relation between inputs and target changes; adaptation is presented as both necessary and hazardous
limitations: Framed over P(X,y); MEYRO's setting is unsupervised with no label stream, so drift semantics must be adapted
meyro_relevance: Directly underpins the adaptation/detection conflict in the problem definition and the design of the Phase 10 adaptive baseline

title: StudentLife: Assessing Mental Health, Academic Performance and Behavioral Trends of College Students using Smartphones
population: 48 Dartmouth students over a 10-week academic term
modalities: Smartphone sensing: accelerometer, GPS, microphone-derived audio features, call and SMS logs, screen state, light; plus EMA self-reports
